correctness.rationale: In the two-block natural-basis structure matrix, only identity and full-cycle terms contribute to the determinant (-1)^n-P, proving precisely the perfect range. In that range pairwise-orthogonality and independence of basis squares force every automorphism monomial. The graph distinguishes the outdegrees and has only rotations. Comparing monomial coefficients gives diagonal subgroup mu_3; the explicitly verified rotating lift has nth power delta_P, and the resulting central group presentation yields C_n x C_3 for P=1 and C_3n otherwise. The full splitting test is an exact calculation in these finite groups. The attached standalone checker independently validates the defining identities, determinant and exhaustive small cases; finite checks are not relied on as general proof.

originality.rationale: The exact six-dimensional nonsplit algebra is already established by Proposition 21 of arXiv:2610.22248v1 and explicitly excluded from novelty. The genuinely new assessed claim is the arbitrary-length, arbitrary cubic-coefficient group classification and the complete P/n splitting boundary, including both split and nonsplit realizations with an identical support graph. The 2026 paper poses a general splitting question, the 2019 foundational paper supplies only the general exact sequence and examples, and the 2022 automorphism classification concerns different graph constructions. Explicit comparisons with the closest previously recorded single oriented-cycle weight classification and live published-index searches found no equivalent covering result, subject to residual implicit-derivation risk.

value.rationale: The exact split/non-split boundary is a structural invariant motivated by Question 33 in arXiv:2610.22248v1. It constructs simple perfect examples of every dimension 2n with 3|n (unbounded), and for odd multiples of three realizes two nonisomorphic automorphism groups on the same directed support graph. This infinite classification and sharp parameter boundary meaningfully extend the isolated n=3 example without claiming a universal answer to Question 33.
